cards.text: Nehemiah, governor of Judah, is telling this one himself. At that time, the Book of Moses is read aloud so all the people can hear it. And in it, they find a passage about two neighboring peoples: the Ammonites and the Moabites.

cards.question: The Book of Moses has a rule about the Ammonites and the Moabites. What does it say?

answers.text: They should never enter the assembly of God
They should be given a share of the land
They should serve as guards at the temple

cards.question: Here's the reason behind the rule. When the Israelites came through long ago, the Ammonites and Moabites met them with food and water. True or false?
No food, no water. Instead, the Ammonites and Moabites hired a man named Balaam to call down a curse against Israel. What did God do with that curse?

answers.text: He turned it into a blessing
He sent it back onto Moab
He let it fall on Balaam

cards.question: The people hear this law from the Book of Moses. They decide to think it over and act on it some other time. True or false?

cards.text: Now back up a little. Before this, Eliashib the priest was put in charge of the storerooms of God's house, and Eliashib is a relative of Tobiah, the Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's wall. Uh-oh.

cards.question: Eliashib runs the storerooms of God's house, and Tobiah is family. What does Eliashib set up for Tobiah?

answers.text: A large room in God's house
A house beside the Fish Gate
A field just outside the city

cards.text: And not just any room. It's where they used to store the grain offerings, the frankincense, the temple articles and the tithes, and friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, and even I know you don't move into the offering room.

cards.question: Nehemiah was right there in Jerusalem when Eliashib gave Tobiah that room. True or false?

cards.text: He'd gone back to Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he finally gets leave to return to Jerusalem, he discovers what Eliashib did for Tobiah. It's like coming home from a long trip and finding out the guy watching your house rented out your BEDROOM.

cards.question: Tobiah is all moved in to a room in the courts of God's house. What does Nehemiah do about it?

answers.text: He throws all of Tobiah's goods out
He lets Tobiah stay if he pays rent
He moves Tobiah to a smaller room

cards.question: Nehemiah was greatly displeased, and Tobiah's household goods are OUT. Speaking as somebody who's been carried off a counter before, I felt that one. What does Nehemiah order next for those rooms?

answers.text: That the rooms be torn down
That the rooms be locked for good

cards.question: Then Nehemiah has the articles of God's house put back in the rooms, along with the grain offerings and ___.

cards.text: Then Nehemiah learns something else: the Levites haven't been given their portions. Imagine going to work every single day, and payday just... never shows up.

cards.question: With no portions coming in, the Levites and singers who served went back to their own ___.
Nehemiah rebukes the officials over the Levites leaving. What question does he ask them?

answers.text: Why has the house of God been neglected
Why has the city wall been left unguarded
Why has the Law of Moses not been read

cards.text: Then he gathers the Levites and singers and puts them back at their posts, and all Judah brings a tenth of the grain, new wine and oil into the storerooms. Tobiah's stuff out, offerings back in: now THAT'S my kind of reorganizing.

cards.question: Nehemiah puts new treasurers over the storerooms: a priest, a scribe, a Levite and a helper. He picks them because they're his relatives. True or false?

cards.text: Then Nehemiah stops right in the middle of his story and prays: "Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out my deeds of loving devotion for the house of my God and for its services."
In those days, Nehemiah sees people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath. They're loading grain, wine, grapes and figs onto donkeys and bringing all kinds of goods into Jerusalem.

cards.question: All those goods are coming into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. So Nehemiah warns the people against ___ food on that day.

cards.text: And it's not just Judah. Men of Tyre living there are importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling it on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem. Day of rest? Not at THIS market.

cards.question: Somebody's getting called out over all this Sabbath trading. Who does Nehemiah rebuke?
Nehemiah reminds the nobles that their forefathers did these same things. So God brought ___ on them and on Jerusalem.

cards.text: And now, he says, they're rekindling God's wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath. Same thing their forefathers did, round two, and Nehemiah is NOT sitting through the rerun.

cards.question: Evening shadows start to fall on Jerusalem's gates, just before the Sabbath. What does Nehemiah order?

answers.text: Shut the gates until after the Sabbath
Light a fire beside every gate
Count every load that comes in

cards.text: He posts some of his own servants at the gates so no load can get in on the Sabbath. Once or twice, the merchants just camp outside Jerusalem, like folks lining up overnight outside a store.

cards.question: Nehemiah does NOT do subtle. He warns the merchants camped in front of the wall. What does he say he'll do if they camp there again?
After Nehemiah's warning, the merchants keep showing up on the Sabbath anyway. True or false?

cards.text: Then he has the Levites purify themselves and guard the gates to keep the Sabbath day holy. And Nehemiah prays again: "Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion."
In those days, Nehemiah also sees Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon and Moab. Yep. Ammon and Moab again.

cards.question: Half of the children from these marriages speak the language of Ashdod or of other peoples. They can't speak the language of ___.

cards.text: Nehemiah rebukes them and calls down curses on them, and he beats some of the men and pulls out their hair. Friend, as a guy who is basically ALL mustache, I am backing away slowly.

cards.question: Then Nehemiah makes the men take an oath before God. What does the oath say?

answers.text: No more marrying into those peoples
No more trading on the Sabbath

cards.question: Nehemiah points the men to a king who sinned in matters like this. There wasn't a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God. Who is he?

cards.text: Yet even Solomon, Nehemiah says, was drawn into sin by foreign women. So he asks them, "Must we now hear that you too are doing all this terrible evil and acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?"

cards.question: Then it hits even closer to home. A grandson of Eliashib the high priest has become a son-in-law to one of Nehemiah's old enemies. Who?

cards.text: That's Sanballat the Horonite, who opposed Nehemiah's wall from the very start. Out of every family on the planet, the high priest's grandson marries into THAT one.

cards.question: Nehemiah lets Sanballat's new son-in-law stay right by his side. True or false?
Nehemiah prays again, but this time it's "Remember them." Remember them for doing what?
So Nehemiah purifies the priests and Levites from everything ___ and assigns specific ___ to each of them.
Nehemiah also arranges for contributions of ___ at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits.

cards.text: And he signs off with one last prayer: "Remember me, O my God, with favor." Storerooms full, gates guarded, priests purified, and the very last thing Nehemiah does is ask God to remember him.
